_meta.purpose: Lexicon for the grounding gate: detect a build-behavior DIAGNOSTIC question about the current project (why does X render/break, where is Y, what's happening with Z) so the agent is forced to read the code + beats BEFORE probing the running app. Consumed by grounding-gate.sh (UserPromptSubmit, arms + injects) and indirectly by grounding-guard.sh (PreToolUse, denies browser/screenshot probes until grounding happened).
_meta.fire_rule: Arm when (a DIAGNOSTIC_FRAME or a BROKEN_STATE phrase) co-occurs with (a BEHAVIOR_VERB or a BUILD_NOUN). Informational framings (what is X / how to use X / explain X / define X) are suppressed, same as the sidecoach hook. Respect the cooldown after a disarm so an active debugging session is not re-nagged.
_meta.why: 2026-06-05: the agent answered 'why aren't my changes showing in the bottom-left panel' by screenshotting/clicking the running app instead of grepping justify/core/changes-panel.ts (which hardcodes bottom:68px;left:20px) and reading the panel beats. The answer was one grep away. This moves the failed CLAUDE.md rule into a mechanical gate (decision_hook_layer_as_enforcement).
_meta.pattern_syntax: Regex fragments, matched case-insensitively against a sanitized prompt (code fences/URLs stripped) with the same hyphen-aware boundaries the sidecoach hook uses. Tune freely - this file is the single source of truth for grounding-gate triggering.
_meta.envelope_measurement: Re-derive these numbers instead of trusting them: `python3 claude/hooks/_tests/measure-hook-corpus.py --gate`. It walks ~/.claude/projects, splits prompts by the structural predicate committed in that file, and prints the fire rate per class. Run 2026-07-28 over 4019 real prompts: 207 fires, of which 124 were a BARE <teammate-message ...> head and 34 were an injected skill body - two envelope shapes the exempt list did not cover, found by measuring rather than by reasoning about it. Roughly a dozen of the remainder are genuine diagnostic questions and SHOULD arm. A handful of prose-headed agent briefs ('Teammate on the X repo...', 'The coordinator sent a message while you were working:') are deliberately NOT exempted: a prose-only head has already been shown to silence a genuine question, and that failure is worse than a few extra nudges.
_meta.envelope_exemption: A prompt that IS an agent/system envelope must never arm the grounding gate: a teammate relay, a task notification, a system reminder, an injected skill body and a context-continuation summary are not the user asking for a diagnosis, but they carry diagnostic prose that matches this lexicon. The earlier '121 of 1231 envelopes (9.83%) versus 13 of 671 genuine (1.94%)' figure is STRUCK - it named a corpus and a split that were never committed, so nobody could re-run it, and it was produced by the same agent that chose the labels. See _meta.envelope_measurement for the re-runnable version. Each pattern requires the STRUCTURAL envelope marker (the literal <teammate-message tag, the <task-notification or <system-reminder element, the skill-injection preamble, the canonical 'ran out of context.' sentence PLUS its Summary section), never merely the opening words - a prose-only head silenced genuine prompts such as 'Another Claude session sent a message saying ... why is the changes panel not showing?'. Matched against the RAW prompt because sanitize() strips <...> tags, after stripping leading BOM/zero-width characters (which are not \s and defeated the ^\s* anchor), and BEFORE the arm and cooldown logic so an envelope can never arm, disarm or burn cooldown.

nudge: This reads as a build-behavior diagnostic question about THIS project. Before you probe the running app (screenshots, clicks, DevTools), GROUND in the source of truth: grep the relevant code path and read the named beats from MEMORY.md. The running app is for VERIFYING an understanding, not forming one - the answer to how the build behaves lives in the code and the beats, usually one grep away. Probing tools (browser/screenshot) are gated until you have read code or beats this turn.
